t: In front of you, opposite the House of Lords in Old Palace Yard, is the statue of George V, King from 1910 until his death in 1936. It was sculpted before the Second World War and hidden in a quarry through the war years. Parliament Square was one suggested site, but it was unveiled here in 1947. The sculptor was Sir William Reid Dick, a Scot who was knighted by George V himself in 1935. The setting was designed by Sir Giles Gilbert Scott, who also designed the iconic red telephone box.
